change_summary: Fixed a routing defect introduced by H-04: global interactive routing kept the excluded /login, /setup and /access-denied pages out of the interactive route table, so the browser replaced them with the 404 template even though the server returned 200.
Components/App.razor now renders static <Routes /> and <HeadOutlet />; the eight interactive pages carry @rendermode InteractiveServer instead.
Added @using static Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web.RenderMode to the root _Imports.razor so per-page render modes resolve.
Recorded the correction and its evidence in docs/DECISIONS_AND_OPEN_GATES.md section 9 and in MVP_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.
No new decision, no scope change and no change to the limited execution authorizations; Phase 3 remains unauthorized.
review_findings: Routing evidence: dotnet build Wizz.sln -c Release = 0 errors; Domain 24/24; Integration 262/262 (286 total).

Browser check on http://localhost:5183: /setup and /login keep their correct content and title after the Blazor circuit connects, with no 404 and no console errors; / redirects to /login and renders the form.

Isolated verification on a temporary SQLite database (deleted afterwards): creating the admin through /setup, logging in, then opening /products, /sales/new, /sales/history, /debts, /reports, /ai and /settings returned full pages with no 404.

Interactivity evidence: each interactive page emits one <!--Blazor:{"type":"server"} marker while /login and /setup emit none, and clicking the new-product button opened a modal without a page reload.

Limitation: the 286 automated tests do not cover browser routing, which is why neither the build nor CI caught this defect; navigation is now a full page load per page and authorization is still evaluated server-side on every request.
